title: Optimising the treatment of chronic ischemic heart disease by training general practitioners to deliver very brief advice on physical activity – work package 6 (pragmatic cluster-randomised controlled trial)
summary:
According to the German care guidelines for the treatment of people with ischemic heart disease, general practitioners should offer their patients with chronic ischemic heart disease advice on physical activity. Brief advice approaches such as the 3As approach (ask/assess the level of physical activity, advise on increasing physical activity and support in the form of specific recommendations (assist), for example) make it easier to implement such advice in everyday general practitioners’ practice. 

Within the OptiCor study, which has been funded by the Federal Ministry of Education and Research since 2022, we have developed a single, 3.5-hour training training for general practitioners in brief advice of patients with ischemic heart disease on physical activity in accordance with the 3As approach. An evaluation study will examine whether this training effectively improves the frequency and quality of general practitioner advice on physical activity.

The study will be conducted in 50 general practitioner practices in North Rhine-Westphalia. The practices will be randomly divided into intervention and control group. For general practitioners of both groups, the training in brief advice to increase physical activity is organised. 

To determine the study endpoints, which are statistically compared between the intervention and control groups:
a)	face-to-face interviews of patients with ischemic heart disease will be conducted over a period of approximately 10 weeks using a questionnaire following the consultation with the general practitioner (n=12 patients/practice; 5 weeks of data collection in the control group, five weeks in the intervention group).
b)	before the training (control group) and in a 14-day period after the training (intervention group), general practitioners’ knowledge, motivation and practical skills in providing advice on physical activity will be assessed using a questionnaire, and
c)	approximately 3 weeks after the general practitioners' training, a process evaluation will be conducted using qualitative interviews (open discussions) with the general practitioners on their experiences with the training, the feasibility of implementing the training content in practice and qualitative short telephone interviews (open discussions) with patients of these general practitioners - if they have received advice on physical activity (including on the experience of this advice, effects, wishes).

interventions.name: Intervention group: General practitioners (GPs) from practices in North Rhine-Westphalia (n=25 practices) will receive a previously developed 3.5- hour training in the provision of brief advice on physical activity (PA, study intervention) according to the 3As brief advice approach (ask/assess physi

Control group: This is the same procedure as in the intervention group (n=25 GP practices). These GPs will also receive the training, but the collection of main outcome data in patients with IHD will take place prior to the training intervention (see also 1.4 study description).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inclusion criteria general practitioners: General practitioners in private practice or employed in North Rhine-Westphalia specialised in general practice, aged 18 and over, who have German language skills and have given written informed consent prior to study inclusion, and who are willing to participate in the 3.5-hour training.

Inclusion criteria patients: All patients with a documented diagnosis of a chronic IHD according to ICD-10 (International Classification of Diseases-10: I25.-I25.9) who personally visit their GP participating in the OptiCor study on the days of data collection and who gave written consent to participate in the study after being approached and informed about the study.
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria general practitioners: Participation in a comparable training or education programme on counselling patients on physical activity (regardless of the disease) within the past five years.

Exclusion criteria patients: severe language barriers, moderate to severe cognitive limitations, significant physical limitations that would massively hinder the performance of physical activity in the sense of sporting activity, as well as explicit instructions from the practice teams not to approach certain people about possible study participation (experience shows that this sometimes happens, for example, in patients with dementia, severe mental illness or an acute situation of the heart disease). Furthermore, no patients without personal contact with a general practitioner on the day of the survey will be included in the study (e.g., if they only pick up a prescription, visit the practice to have their blood taken or visit a relative).
